clauses.reason: Terminated by Executive Order 12553, signed February 25, 1986 and published at 51 FR 7237 in the Federal Register of March 3, 1986. Its enacting sentence orders that the listed Executive Orders, and "any amendments thereto", are revoked; the text states no delayed effective date and contains no saving clause, so the effective date is the signing date, 1986-02-25 (the printed date, March 3, 1986, is the alternative reading). The table of revoked orders in the held text of Executive Order 12553 lists number 11321 with the subject "Creating a board of inquiry to report on a labor dispute affecting the military aircraft engine industry". This order (31 FR 16301, Federal Register of December 21, 1966, signed December 19, 1966) created, under section 206 of the Labor-Management Relations Act of 1947 (61 Stat. 155; 29 U.S.C. 176), a Board of Inquiry of three named members (Laurence E. Seibel as chairman, Frank J. Dugan and Garth L. Mangum) to inquire into the issues in the labor dispute between the Union Carbide Corporation and certain of its employees represented by the United Steelworkers of America, AFL-CIO, and Local Union No. 2958 thereof, involving the Stellite Division plant at Kokomo, Indiana, a dispute that had resulted in a strike affecting the military aircraft engine industry; gave the Board the powers and duties set forth in Title II of the Act; directed it to report to the President in accordance with section 206 on or before December 20, 1966; and provided that upon submission of its report the Board shall continue in existence to perform such other functions as may be required under the Act. The report date is a deadline, not an end, under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines (option C), and the continuing-existence sentence means the order's own text does not end the Board at the report. No report of this Board is held among the sources cited by the dossier, so no report date is recorded; the clause is described only as functionally spent as to its reporting deadline, and the order stayed on the books until this express revocation.

research_rationale:
Identity: the held Federal Register text (31 FR 16301, the issue of December 21, 1966) is Executive Order 11321, dated December 19, 1966; it is headed with the title Creating a Board of Inquiry to Report on a Labor Dispute Affecting the Military Aircraft Engine Industry of the United States, names the Union Carbide Corporation dispute, and is dated December 19, 1966. The dossier's clause inventory for this order covers neighbouring Federal Register documents, not this order, so I replaced it with the order's own operative text. I read the whole order; the representation is the machine-extracted text layer of the official PDF (OCR for this period), and I did not inspect the page images. End: express revocation by Executive Order 12553 on 1986-02-25. Searches: current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog, each marked complete in the dossier.

The held-text number search for this order found no held later order that cites it other than Executive Order 12553, and my reading of the held text of Executive Order 12553 shows no earlier revoking, superseding or terminating instrument.","independent_command_check":"Each command (create and appoint the Board, state its powers by reference to Title II of the Act, set the report deadline, continue the Board in existence) depends on this order and on the one dispute it addressed; the Board's statutory powers come from the Labor-Management Relations Act, a separate statute.","savings_check":"Executive Order 12553 was read in full: it consists of one revoking sentence, a table of the revoked orders by number and subject, an editorial note and the signature block, and it contains no saving or transition provision. The Board's statutory functions under the Labor-Management Relations Act are those of the Act itself and the dispute was a one-time dispute.","scope_check":"One clause is inventoried by correction: the whole operative text (the recitals of the dispute and strike, the creation and membership of the Board, its powers and duties, the report deadline and the continuing-existence sentence). savings.reason: Executive Order 12553, read in full, contains no saving or transition provision: its text is one revoking sentence, a table of the revoked orders, an editorial note and the signature block. The Board's statutory functions under the Labor-Management Relations Act are those of the Act itself and the dispute was a one-time dispute. No held claim-grade source shows any command of this order continuing when it was revoked.
